reporting-org.narrative: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

title.narrative: Middle East Response - Ensuring continuity of treatment and essential services for people affected by HIV, TB and malaria in Yemen, Syria, Iraq, Jordan and Lebanon - Western Asia - Multicountry Middle East MER (01-Jan-2019-31-Dec-2021)

description.narrative: Multicountry Middle East MER, Multicomponent, International Organization for Migration (IOM)This program has the following goals: To continue to provide essential HIV, TB, and malaria services to eligible country populations in Syria, Yemen and Iraq and to Syrian refugees and vulnerable populations in Jordan and Lebanon.. To build on the achievments of MER 1 scaling up identified interventions for impact. To prevent collapse of service delivery for the three diseases in countries affected by conflict and humanitarian crises and continue to strenghten local health systems. The objectives of this program are: In Yemen, ensure access to malaria prevention, diagnosis and treatment prioritising vulnerable populations (IDPs, Refugees, malnourished, children under 5 years of age and pregnant women); protect at-risk populations with LLINs and strengthen surevillance, epidemic detection, preparedness and response; to scale up integrated community case management of malaria in high-risk settings. In Yemen, Syria and Iraq: Ensure access to tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment prioritising vulnerable populations (IDPs, Refugees, malnourished, children and pregnant women); to improve and strenghten tuberculosis contact management; to increase involvement of community workers for tuberculosis care and prevention; to increase access to diagnosis and treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis; to increase access of tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment to PLHIV and vice versa.. In Yemen, Syria and Lebanon: Ensure access to HIV prevention, diagnosis, care, support and treatment to PLHIV prioritising key populations; improve treatment coverage in key populations from 26% to 40%; enhance HTS through innovative and high-yield approaches within the current security context. For Syrian refugees and vulnerable populations in Jordan and Lebanon: Ensure access to tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment; to improve and strenghten tuberculosis contact management; to increase involvement of community workers for tuberculosis care and prevention; to increase access to diagnosis and treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis; to increase access of tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment to PLHIV and vice versa. For Syrian refugees and vulnerable populations in Jordan: Ensure access to HIV prevention, diagnosis, care, support and treatment to PLHIV prioritising key populations; improve treatment coverage in key populations; enhance HTS through innovative and high-yield approaches through partnerships with CBOs and NGOs
